text:
alina: quick question — trying to disable client metrics from the python SDK for a compliance test. set REDWOOD_CLIENT_METRICS=0 but still see :bar_chart: events in our proxy logs. anyone run into this?
morgan: are you on the latest 0.4.x client? we changed env var names in 0.4.1.
alina: yep 0.4.1 pinned in requirements.txt. I also tried client.disable_metrics() after init, no luck.
tj: what headers are you seeing? can you paste request sample (no tokens)?
alina: sure — minimal headers we send:```
{'User-Agent': 'my-app/1.2.3 python-requests/2.31.0',
 'Authorization': 'Bearer <redacted>',
 'X-Redwood-Telemetry': 'enabled'}
```
alina: I *think* server is treating presence of X-Redwood-Telemetry as opt-in. I removed it and saw metrics stop for a bit, but they came back after a retry.
morgan: ah — interesting. current behavior: server-side will honor client opt-out *if* the opt-out header is explicit. the SDK previously set a telemetry header for feature flags which could accidentally re-enable. the fix is to send x-redwood-telemetry-optout: true OR remove the telemetry header entirely.
sandeep: for python specifically, our lib sets telemetry flag if APPLICATION_NAME is provided in UA. So if your UA includes pattern `redwood-*`, it auto-enables extra fields.
alina: ugh — that explains it. we populate UA with our service id so it included `redwood-service`. quick question: what should UA look like to keep us identifiable but not trigger telemetry?
tj: recommended UA format: `redwood-sdk/<version> <app-name>/<version>` — avoid `redwood-service` token. example: `redwood-sdk-python/0.4.1 my-service/1.2.3`.
devex-bot: docs: https://redwood.internal/docs/sdk/telemetry#user-agent-and-headers
morgan: on tracing propagation — the SDK supports W3C `traceparent`. If you pass `traceparent` header it will be propagated to backend logs and not mutated. Example: `traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01`.
alina: did you mean `traceparent` rather than `x-redwood-trace`? we've been adding a custom header to correlate spans.
sandeep: prefer `traceparent`. our observability expects W3C header. we still ingest custom headers but they can create duplicates and weird sampling.
alina: thanks — switching to traceparent now.
morgan: one more streaming quirk: when a streaming request fails mid-stream (connection reset), the client will not automatically retry the same stream payload. you need to re-open stream and replay prompt with model-aware resume (e.g., using model KV cache). for short user-facing streams we recommend exponential backoff and resume token if you have it.
tj: implement backoff like: initial 200ms, factor 2, max 5s, max attempts 4. and avoid retrying user-visible messages more than once.
alina: noted. are there language differences for disabling metrics (node vs python)?
sandeep: node sets opt-out via header by default if process.env.REDWOOD_CLIENT_METRICS === '0'. python reads env var and env var override is lowest precedence — method call > header > env var. so call client.disable_metrics() after init to be sure.
alina: perfect. I'll remove the telemetry header, add explicit `x-redwood-telemetry-optout: true`, and switch to `traceparent`. will follow up if metrics still show up. thanks all :heart:
morgan: ping me if you want a quick PR review for the client patch.
end of thread
